newsitem.title: UK: European heating oil slumps as U.S. supply hits.
newsitem.headline: European heating oil slumps as U.S. supply hits.

text.p: European gas oil prices slumped $5/6 per tonne as heavy selling hit the IPE futures market and traders perceived more heating oil supply.
They said two or three Russian cargoes were on offer and heating oil premiums were hit by a large amount of U.S. material being offered in Europe, but European diesel stayed firm.
IPE October futures dropped $5.00 to $226.75 per tonne by 1200 GMT.
French heating oil premiums slumped by around $2.00/3.00 and Russian premiums lost $1.00/2.00 as they faced increased competition from U.S. cargoes.
A French heating oil cargo was offered at Oct +$5.00, but attracted interest only at a $1.00/2.00 premium.

While some U.S. cargoes had very low sulphur, some as low as 0.03 percent, they did not conform to Europeanm cetane specs and only fetched heating oil prices. U.S. cargoes were offered at between Oct +$2.00 and $7.00, depending on quality and timing, and most cargoes were restricted to deep ports.
By contrast, low sulphur European diesel continued to find strong support, with several buyers still looking for material into Germany and cargo premiums held up around $18 cif.
